clue.text: Not understanding dumping, hence Ron elaborated

indicators.note: elaborated means worked up into a new form, so these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone baffled because Ron has embroidered his account of rubbish being dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elaborated' signals rearranging the letters of DUMPING, HENCE and RON together.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to grasp something is to be without comprehension, a plain synonym.

clue.text: The importance of X cannot be foreseen

definitions.text: The importance of X cannot be foreseen

parts.words: The importance of X cannot be foreseen
parts.note: in algebra X stands for a value not yet known; the phrase also describes a person or thing whose significance cannot be predicted

explanation.surface: A remark that some factor X's significance is impossible to predict.
explanation.walkthrough: X is the conventional letter for the value an equation is solving for, so the clue reads both as algebra and as a figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a mathematical variable and, figuratively, a person or factor whose effect is unpredictable.

clue.text: Was anxious about a left-winger

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
a red is a socialist or communist, a left-winger

explanation.surface: Someone worried about a socialist colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: To have cared is to have felt concern or worry, a synonym of being anxious.

clue.text: Younger boy with one in a raincoat coming from the lodge

indicators.note: in tells us the boy and the one sit inside the raincoat

parts.note: a mac (mackintosh) is a raincoat
a son is a boy of the younger generation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A young lad in a mac emerges from a building called the lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: A Freemasons' meeting place is called a lodge, which the surface disguises as an ordinary house.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons meet in lodges, so something from the lodge is Masonic.

clue.text: Radical said to have gone first and searched vigorously

parts.note: radical comes from the Latin for root; a root is the radical part
to have led is to have gone first, at the head

explanation.surface: A radical who reportedly went ahead and hunted hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said to have' only joins the pieces: LED is what one is said to have done in going first.
explanation.definitionFit: Rootled is a British variant of rooted, to dig about or rummage energetically.

clue.text: Cautious with flue he'd moved

indicators.note: moved means the letters are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: A careful chimney-sweep has shifted the flue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' signals rearranging FLUE and HED (the apostrophe in he'd gives no letter).
explanation.definitionFit: Being careful and attentive is a synonym of paying heed, mindful.

clue.text: Scoring in football but not in tennis

definitions.text: Scoring in football but not in tennis

parts.words: Scoring in football but not in tennis
parts.note: putting the ball in the net wins a goal in football, but in tennis hitting it into the net loses the point

explanation.surface: A comparison of how points are won in two ball games.
explanation.definitionFit: Finding the net is a goal in football but a fault in tennis, so the one word covers both.

clue.text: In an awkward situation behind the horse

definitions.meaning: literally riding in the wagon a horse draws

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a fix, riding behind a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in trouble; taken literally a cart sits behind its horse.

clue.text: Is one not particularly ill staying here?

definitions.text: Is one not particularly ill staying here?

parts.words: Is one not particularly ill staying here?
parts.note: general is read as the opposite of particular, so a patient not ill in any particular way stays there

explanation.surface: A question about whether a mildly sick person should be in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is 'not particularly': general and particular are opposites, giving the name of a non-specialist hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-specialist hospital treats all kinds of ailments rather than one particular kind.

clue.text: Broken set mended at the edge of the pavement

indicators.note: mended means put back together differently, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A broken set of crockery gets repaired on the pavement's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' is fodder, not the indicator; 'mended' rearranges BROKEN and SET.
explanation.definitionFit: The stones lining a pavement's border form the curb, called kerb in Britain.

clue.text: Giant has the item in brown

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the brown

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
it means the item, the thing mentioned

explanation.surface: A giant keeps some item inside a brown container.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titans were giants, and the word means any huge figure.

clue.text: It might be the first service book

definitions.meaning: a number such as first, second or third showing position in a series
a book giving the forms of church services, such as ordination

explanation.surface: Something that could be first, or a book of church services.
explanation.definitionFit: First is a positional number, and the same word names a book of church rites.

clue.text: Hairdresser to stand up amid some, thick fine hair

indicators.note: amid places the standing up in the middle of the hair

parts.note: fur is the thick fine hair of animals
to rise is to stand up

explanation.surface: A hairdresser stands up among some thick, fine hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Friseur is the French-derived word for a hairdresser.

clue.text: It cannot fly in the museum

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A flightless exhibit stands in the museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian bird is large and flightless.

clue.text: Saw it had thawed

explanation.surface: Someone saw that the ice had melted.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is read in two words, NOT ICED, meaning thawed.
explanation.definitionFit: To have spotted something is to have seen it; split in two the word says no longer frozen.

clue.text: Union day lady's outfit

parts.note: a union is a marriage, so the clothes a bride gathers for her wedding

explanation.surface: Clothes a woman wears on a day of union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' sounds like a trade union or political union but means a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride traditionally assembles a collection of clothes and linen for her marriage.

clue.text: And in France a letter from another country

parts.note: et is the French for and

explanation.surface: A French conjunction plus an article, and a letter from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a letter of the Greek alphabet, foreign to English.

clue.text: Ball e.g. I spun on the wicket

indicators.note: spun suggests turning about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bowler spins a ball on the cricket wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket two small bails sit on top of the stumps; the one nearer the batter's legs side is the leg bail.
explanation.definitionFit: This bail is one of the two small pieces resting on top of the cricket stumps.

clue.text: Measure pound note first then another pound

parts.note: E is a musical note
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)
a second L for pound

explanation.surface: Measuring out banknotes and coins: a pound note, then another pound.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old unit of length for cloth.

clue.text: More perfect

parts.note: Thomas More wrote of an ideal commonwealth, so this is perfect in More's way as well as an adjective for idealized

explanation.surface: Something improved, more perfect than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' looks like a comparative but is Sir Thomas More, author of a book about an ideal island.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealistically perfect, after More's imaginary ideal state.

clue.text: A very cold sheet

parts.note: a sheet here is a flat expanse of frozen sea water, not bedding

explanation.surface: Bedding that is chilly to the touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating flat expanse of frozen sea is a frozen sheet.

clue.text: Cannot be distinguished

explanation.surface: A claim that two things cannot be told apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be distinguished' looks like 'be told apart', but 'distinguished' means eminent and 'be' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Split, the word means unable; whole, it means remarkable or eminent.

clue.text: Voter turns tail on seeing a printing plate

indicators.note: the tail, the last two letters of the voter word, are turned round

parts.note: an elector is a voter

explanation.surface: A voter flees at the sight of a printing plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns tail' looks like running away, but it reverses only the last two letters, OR becoming RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for electrotype, a metal copy of type used for printing.

clue.text: Mournful for instance after the French returning across

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Mournful for instance after the French returning across' gives EL + EG but nothing in it supplies the I before AC; a word appears lost in OCR and no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: Mournful for instance after the French returning across

clue.text: Arrangement of one record is by a foreign character

indicators.note: an arrangement re-orders the letters of the words that follow

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a single record for a foreign singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement of' shuffles ONE, LP and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character from another script.

clue.text: Singularly well-produced work of art

parts.note: a substance drawn up from a well, and used singly for a painting made in that medium

explanation.surface: Praise for an unusually well-made artwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-produced' means pumped from a well; 'Singularly' says the word is used in the singular for one painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum comes from wells, and a painting in that medium is called by the same word.

clue.text: Being born on a North American trail

parts.note: a scent is a trail followed by hounds

explanation.surface: A newborn on a North American hiking trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just coming into existence is newly emerging.

clue.text: Became less severe as Dee struggled up

indicators.note: struggled suggests twisting about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Things improved as the River Dee fought its way upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggled' rearranges AS and DEE; the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken or moderate is to become gentler.

clue.text: Physician to take off the cover

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor, a physician
to ape is to mimic, take off

explanation.surface: A doctor removing a patient's covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like remove, but it means imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape is a cloth hung over something, a covering.

clue.text: Perfect model

definitions.meaning: an example to aim at, as a noun

explanation.surface: An exemplary model.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means flawless as an adjective and a standard to aspire to as a noun.

clue.text: Sparklingly clever?

parts.note: a diamond cut to sparkle bears this name, and the adjective means very clever

explanation.surface: A compliment on someone's dazzling intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means exceptionally clever and also a sparkling cut diamond.

clue.text: At no time is the second person able to discern that appearances are deceptive

parts.note: you is the second-person pronoun
never means at no time
can means is able
to tell is to discern or make out

explanation.surface: A statement that one can never judge by looks.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in a different order from the clue: the second person first, then 'At no time'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying means things may not be what they seem.
